8	#### Properties of the subalgebra relation for setoid algebras
9	
10	This is the [Setoid.Subalgebras.Properties][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
11	
12	This module establishes the order-theoretic facts about the subalgebra relation
13	`_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} that the rest of the library relies on: that it is a
14	preorder, that isomorphism refines it in either direction, that it survives
15	universe lifting, and that it is preserved by products.
16	
17	The preorder is stated with respect to isomorphism rather than equality
18	(`≤-preorder`{.AgdaFunction}), which is the only sensible choice, since mutual
19	embeddings do not make two algebras equal.  The universe-lifting group is the
20	part used most often, for the reason recorded in [Setoid.Algebras.Basic][]:
21	Agda's universes are not cumulative, so a `≤` established at one level has to be
22	transported explicitly before it can be used at another.
23

137	#### Lifts of subalgebras of setoid algebras
138	
139	Ten lemmas of one shape: transport a `≤` or a `≥` across the isomorphism between
140	an algebra and its lift.  The seven one-sided ones are each a single application
141	of a mixed transitivity lemma from above to one of the `Lift-≅`{.AgdaFunction}
142	isomorphisms of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Isomorphisms][]; the three
143	`Lift-≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} variants then compose two of those.  Either way no
144	lemma is more than a line, which is the concrete sense in which universe lifting
145	costs nothing here.
146	
147	The suffix says which level moves, following `Lift-Algˡ`{.AgdaFunction},
148	`Lift-Algʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and `Lift-Alg`{.AgdaFunction} of
149	[Setoid.Algebras.Basic][]: `ˡ` raises the level of the carrier, `ʳ` the level of
150	the equality, and the unadorned name raises both.
151	
152	+  `≤-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `≤-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
153	   `≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} lift the algebra on the right of `≤`, the larger one;
154	+  `≥-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `≥-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
155	   `≥-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} do the same for `≥`, which lifts the smaller one;
156	+  `Lift-≤-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `Lift-≤-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
157	   `Lift-≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} lift both algebras at once, and are literally the
158	   composition of the two groups above;
159	+  `Lift-is-sub`{.AgdaFunction} is the class-relative version: lifting an algebra
160	   does not disturb its being a subalgebra of some member of `𝒦`.
161	
162	```agda

164	  {𝒦 : Pred (Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ)(ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} α)}
165	  {𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} {ℓ : Level}
166	  → 𝑩 ≤c 𝒦 → (Lift-Algˡ 𝑩 ℓ) ≤c 𝒦
167	Lift-is-sub (𝑨 , (KA , B≤A)) = 𝑨 , (KA , A≥B×B≅C→A≥C B≤A Lift-≅ˡ)

171	  ≤-Liftˡ A≤B = A≤B×B≅C→A≤C A≤B Lift-≅ˡ

200	#### Products of subalgebras
201	
202	`⨅-≤`{.AgdaFunction} is the compatibility of the subalgebra relation with
203	products: if `ℬ i ≤ 𝒜 i` for every index `i`, then `⨅ ℬ ≤ ⨅ 𝒜`.  The embedding is
204	assembled coordinatewise from the given ones, and injectivity is coordinatewise
205	too, because two elements of a product are equal exactly when they agree in every
206	coordinate.
207	
208	Small as it is, this is the load-bearing step of `PS⊆SP`{.AgdaFunction} in
209	[Setoid.Varieties.Preservation][], where a product of subalgebras has to be
210	recognised as a subalgebra of a product so that `S`{.AgdaFunction} and
211	`P`{.AgdaFunction} can be interchanged.
212	
213	```agda
214	module _
215	  {I : Type ι}
216	  {𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}
217	  {ℬ : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}
218	  where
219	  open IsHom
220	
221	  ⨅-≤ : (∀ i → ℬ i ≤ 𝒜 i) → ⨅ ℬ ≤ ⨅ 𝒜
222	  ⨅-≤ B≤A = h , hM
223	    where
224	    h : hom (⨅ ℬ) (⨅ 𝒜)
225	    h = hfunc , hhom
226	      where
227	      homAt : ∀ i → hom (ℬ i) (𝒜 i)
228	      homAt = λ i → proj₁ (B≤A i)
229	
230	      hmapAt : ∀ i → 𝔻[ ℬ i ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝒜 i ]
231	      hmapAt = proj₁ ∘ homAt
232	
233	      hfunc : 𝔻[ ⨅ ℬ ] ⟶ 𝔻[ ⨅ 𝒜 ]
234	      hfunc ⟨$⟩ x = λ i → (hmapAt i) ⟨$⟩ (x i)
235	      hfunc .cong = λ xy i → cong (hmapAt i) (xy i)
236	
237	      hhom : IsHom (⨅ ℬ) (⨅ 𝒜) hfunc
238	      hhom .compatible = λ i → compatible (proj₂ (homAt i))
239	
240	    hM : IsInjective (proj₁ h)
241	    hM = λ xy i → (proj₂ (B≤A i)) (xy i)
242	```

51	
52	#### Subdirect products and subdirect embeddings
53	
54	Fix a candidate algebra `𝑩` and a factor family `𝒜`.  The `i`-th **coordinate map**
55	of a homomorphism `h : 𝑩 → ⨅ 𝒜` is the composite `projᵢ ∘ h : 𝑩 → 𝒜 i`.
56	The homomorphism `h : 𝑩 → ⨅ 𝒜` is a **subdirect embedding** when it is injective and
57	every coordinate map is surjective.
58	
59	```agda
60	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{I : Type ι}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}(𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ) where
61	
62	  -- The i-th coordinate map projᵢ ∘ h of a hom into the product.
63	  coord : hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜) → (i : I) → hom 𝑩 (𝒜 i)
64	  coord h i = ⊙-hom h (⨅-proj 𝒜 i)
65	
66	  record IsSubdirectEmbedding (h : hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜)) : Type (ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ) where
67	    field
68	      embed-inj  : IsInjective (proj₁ h)
69	      proj-onto  : (i : I) → IsSurjective (proj₁ (coord h i))
70	
71	  open IsSubdirectEmbedding public
72	
73	  -- A subdirect embedding of 𝑩 into ⨅ 𝒜;  i.e., 𝑩 is a subdirect product of 𝒜.
74	  SubdirectEmbedding : Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ ι ⊔ α ⊔ ρ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ)
75	  SubdirectEmbedding = Σ[ h ∈ hom 𝑩 (⨅ 𝒜) ] IsSubdirectEmbedding h
76	
77	  -- A subdirect embedding is in particular a subalgebra inclusion 𝑩 ≤ ⨅ 𝒜.
78	  subdirect→≤ : SubdirectEmbedding → 𝑩 ≤ ⨅ 𝒜
79	  subdirect→≤ (h , emb) = h , embed-inj emb
80	```

82	#### The bridge: a separating family of congruences gives a subdirect embedding
83	
84	Now the constructive heart.  Fix an algebra `𝑨` and a family of congruences
85	`θ : I → Con 𝑨`.  Form the family of quotients `i ↦ 𝑨 ╱ θ i` and the natural map
86	into their product, assembled from the canonical quotient projections `πhom (θ i)`.
87	
88	```agda
89	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{I : Type ι}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ}(θ : I → Con 𝑨 ℓ) where
90	  -- the family of quotient algebras and the natural map into their product
91	  𝑨╱ : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ℓ
92	  𝑨╱ i = 𝑨 ╱ θ i
93
